title: U.S. House · Missouri's 5th District
area: Kansas City and eastern Jackson County, including the urban core of Kansas City and Independence.

context.text: Incumbent Emanuel Cleaver ran unopposed in the August 4, 2026 Democratic primary. Rick Brattin won a six-candidate Republican primary over Micah Beebe, Taylor Burks, Brett Hueffmeier, Berton A. Knox and Brad Patty. Randy Langkraehr advanced unopposed in the Libertarian primary.

candidates.name: Emanuel Cleaver

summary.text: Emanuel Cleaver is the incumbent Democratic U.S. Representative for Missouri's 5th District. A retired United Methodist pastor who served as mayor of Kansas City from 1991 to 1999, he sits on the House Financial Services Committee.

background.text: Born in Waxahachie, Texas, in 1944; earned a bachelor's degree in sociology from Prairie View A&M University (1972) and a Master of Divinity from St. Paul School of Theology (1974).
Served as Senior Pastor at St. James United Methodist Church in Kansas City from 1973 to 2009.
Served on the Kansas City City Council from 1979 to 1991, then as mayor of Kansas City from 1991 to 1999, the city's first African American mayor.

priorities.text: Says the country needs to invest in clean-energy technologies such as solar, wind, geothermal and hydropower as part of a long-term energy strategy, and has continually supported the Low Income Home Energy Assistance Program (LIHEAP).
Says Congress should focus on rebuilding an economy that works for everyone, including investments in job creation and education, rather than cuts to programs supporting struggling families.

positions.summary: Supports investing in clean, renewable energy technologies as part of the nation's energy strategy.
positions.quote: We must invest in clean-energy generating technologies such as solar, wind, geothermal and hydropower as part of a long-term, ecologically sound energy strategy.

positions.summary: Supports raising the federal minimum wage and tying it to inflation.
positions.quote: We need to raise the minimum wage and tie it to inflation so that a family breadwinner's pay keeps up with the rising costs of housing and other basic needs.

record.text: Serves on the House Committee on Financial Services in the 119th Congress (2025-2026); previously served as Ranking Member of its Housing and Insurance Subcommittee (2023-2024).

candidates.researchNotes: Cleaver ran unopposed in the Democratic primary; no 2026 Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey was located. His official House issues subpages (energy, economy and jobs, financial services, foreign affairs, agriculture, education) were fetched directly; most content is several years old and largely does not address the guide's 15 issue statements directly, apart from the energy and minimum-wage positions above. candidates.name: Rick Brattin
candidates.ballotNote: Won a six-candidate August 4, 2026 Republican primary

summary.text: Rick Brattin is the Republican nominee for Missouri's 5th District. A Missouri state senator and former state representative from Harrisonville, he is campaigning as an ally of President Trump on gun rights, opposition to abortion, and immigration enforcement.

background.text: Lives in Harrisonville, Missouri; graduated from Lee's Summit High School and served in the U.S. Marine Corps.
Career experience includes owning and operating a construction company and a farm before serving in the Missouri House and Missouri Senate.

priorities.text: Campaign website describes him as "a strong ally for the administration," citing a record of sponsoring legislation to advance President Trump's agenda in the Missouri legislature.

positions.summary: Campaign website says he helped craft Missouri's constitutional protections for the Second Amendment and voted for the state's Second Amendment Preservation Act; says he'll oppose any attempt to infringe on gun rights in Congress.

Campaign website says he voted to extend Missouri's abortion waiting period to 72 hours and backed a bill requiring parental notice before a minor's abortion; says he'll fight to defund Planned Parenthood in Congress.
positions.quote: Rick is 100% pro-life with a consistent record to prove it.

positions.summary: Campaign website says he sponsored state legislation penalizing companies that hire undocumented workers and fought to ban sanctuary cities; says he'll back fully funding ICE and deporting people in the country illegally with criminal records.

record.text: As a Missouri legislator, sponsored bills to prevent government entities from contracting with companies that discriminate against firearms manufacturers, and voted for the state's Second Amendment Preservation Act.
Voted to extend Missouri's abortion waiting period from 24 to 72 hours and backed a bill requiring parents of minors seeking an abortion to receive five days' notice.
Sponsored legislation imposing penalties on companies that hire undocumented workers without verifying immigration status and worked to ban sanctuary cities in Missouri.

candidates.researchNotes: No 2026 Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey completed; positions drawn from his campaign website as reproduced by Ballotpedia. His Missouri Senate voting record is otherwise not independently verified here.
